questions.q: Why is science described as an 'ever-evolving' body of knowledge?
answer: Science is called ever-evolving because its ideas are not fixed but keep growing and changing as new evidence is found.

answer.text: Science is a way of knowing built through observation, questioning, experiment and reasoning. Every idea is tested against evidence rather than accepted on authority.
When new observations do not fit an existing idea, scientists revise or replace it. In this way science corrects itself over time, and older explanations give way to better ones.
Because there is always more to observe and test, science never stands still. Curiosity and careful investigation keep it advancing, which is why it is described as ever-evolving.

questions.q: Describe the steps of the scientific method and what makes an experiment fair.
answer: The scientific method is the systematic way scientists investigate a question.

answer.text: It begins with observing something and asking a question, then forming a hypothesis, a testable guess that might answer it. The hypothesis is tested by experiment, the results are recorded and analysed, and a conclusion is drawn, after which the test is repeated to be sure.
For an experiment to be fair, only one factor should be changed at a time while all others are kept the same. This way any difference in the result can be linked to that one factor.

answer: Throughout, science depends on evidence and measurement rather than opinion.
